$comment: Ground truth for the ShopFlow benchmark application (sample-ecommerce-app/).
DO NOT READ THIS FILE WHILE TESTING THE APPLICATION. It exists to score a run after
the fact, not to inform one. Every defect below used to be labelled in the application's
own source with an `INJECTED ...` comment, which meant `grep -rn INJECTED` found all
eight without testing anything -- an 8/8 detection rate that measured grep, not the agent.
Line numbers are a convenience and will drift. `anchor` is the stable identifier: match
on it, not on the line.
Scoring: a defect counts as DETECTED only when the agent reports the observable symptom
with execution evidence. Naming the line without demonstrating the behaviour is not a
detection -- it is a code review, which this benchmark does not measure.
application_commit_note: Regenerate the database with `npm run seed` before a run; data.sqlite is not committed.

defects.title: Broken object-level authorization (IDOR) on order detail
defects.anchor: GET /:id handler -- `const items = db.prepare(` immediately after the 404 check
defects.defect: The handler authenticates the caller but never checks that the order belongs to them. A check of the form `order.user_id !== req.user.id && req.user.role !== 'admin'` is missing entirely.
defects.observable_symptom: Authenticate as user 2 (Bob) and request an order belonging to user 1 (Alice). The API returns 200 with Alice's order, shipping address and line items.

defects.title: Cart accepts negative and fractional quantities
defects.defect: Validation checks the type of `quantity` but not its value. `Number.isInteger(quantity) && quantity > 0` is missing.
defects.observable_symptom: POST an item with `quantity: -2`. It is accepted, and the cart subtotal decreases -- a negative line total that can be used to drive the order total down.

defects.title: Coupon minimum-spend boundary is exclusive, not inclusive
defects.defect: The coupon contract is "valid for purchases of $X or more", so the comparison must be `>=`. It is `>`, an off-by-one on the boundary value.
defects.observable_symptom: A subtotal exactly equal to `min_spend` (e.g. $50.00 against a $50 minimum) receives no discount, while $50.01 does.
defects.note: The only defect reachable by pure unit testing. The shipped suite in backend/test/pricing.test.js passes without catching it -- it never tests the boundary.

defects.title: Checkout deducts one unit of stock regardless of quantity ordered
defects.anchor: checkout loop -- `UPDATE products SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE id = ?`
defects.defect: The decrement is hardcoded to 1 instead of binding `item.quantity`.
defects.observable_symptom: Order 5 units of a product with stock 10. The order succeeds and stock becomes 9, not 5. Repeated orders oversell the inventory.

defects.title: Pagination offset skips the first page of products
defects.defect: Page numbers are 1-based, so the offset must be `(page - 1) * limit`.
defects.observable_symptom: GET /api/products with no query string (page defaults to 1) starts at offset 10. The first ten products are unreachable through the API.

defects.title: Missing product returns 200 OK instead of 404
defects.defect: A missing entity is answered with 200 and a null payload, violating the REST contract the rest of the API follows (orders.js returns 404 correctly).
defects.observable_symptom: GET /api/products/99999 returns 200 with `{ success: false, product: null }`. A client checking only the status code treats the product as found.

defects.title: Cart badge counts distinct lines, and checkout can be double-submitted
defects.defect: Two related front-end defects. The badge shows the number of distinct cart lines rather than the summed quantity. Separately, `handleCheckoutSubmit` (app.js:347) never disables the submit button, so rapid clicks fire duplicate orders.
defects.observable_symptom: Add 3 units of one product: the badge reads 1, not 3. Click 'Place Order Now' twice quickly: two orders are created.

defects.title: Unlabelled controls and insufficient colour contrast
defects.anchor: checkout form -- card inputs with placeholder only
defects.defect: Three WCAG failures. The card number, expiry and CVV inputs have no label and no aria-label (WCAG 3.3.2 / 4.1.2). The cart remove button is a bare glyph with no accessible name (4.1.2). `.low-contrast-text` renders #4ade80 on white at roughly 2.1:1, below the 4.5:1 required for normal text (1.4.3).
defects.observable_symptom: An accessibility scan or screen-reader pass reports unnamed form controls and a contrast violation on the order-confirmation text.

additional_sites.anchor: cart remove button -- glyph with no accessible name

known_blind_spots: Eight defects is a small, hand-authored sample. A high score here is evidence the machinery works on these eight, not a detection rate that generalises.
Every defect was written to be findable. There are no defects that require load, timing, concurrency or long-running state to reproduce.
The sample is biased toward the backend: five of eight are API-reachable, which favours api-testing over the UI categories.

Because the application ships with a passing unit suite that misses all eight, a run that only executes the existing suite scores zero. That is the intended lesson, but it means the benchmark rewards exploration specifically.
